# PHASE-003 - Define delegated orchestration lifecycle

| Field | Value |

## Objective

Implement role-governed solver, reviewer, synthesis, conflict, implementation-owner, and completion stages, with supporting-package edits only where impact evidence requires them.

## Scope

- Role selection and creation for orchestration functions
- Independent candidate solutions
- One-to-one review and revision
- Senior synthesis and conflict recycling
- Final implementation ownership and completion
- Conditional Agent Task and Manage Sub-Agent Roles changes

## Entry conditions

- PHASE-002 is complete.
- Q-001's approved answer is available to TASK-010.
- The impact matrix controls conditional supporting-package edits.

## Exit criteria

- Every orchestration stage has a bounded owner, gate, durable record, and stopping condition.
- Exactly one implementation owner is recorded before execution.
- Conditional package changes or no-change dispositions are complete and verified.

## Risks

- Repeated edits to shared core documents require strict task ordering.
- Conditional supporting-package changes could introduce unnecessary schema or compatibility work.

Extend the reusable Task and Director contracts so solver, reviewer, senior synthesizer, and implementer assignments all use a fresh role catalog, complete task profiles, the narrowest valid role, verified skill and tool availability, exact inheritance, bounded delegation contracts, and role creation only for a reusable role gap.

### Risks

- The new orchestration labels could bypass the existing role-management workflow.
- A missing capability could be mislabeled as a reusable role gap.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every delegated function uses a fresh valid role catalog and a task profile containing objective, capabilities, read and write needs, expected output, required skills, tools, risk, and stopping condition.
- Each delegation names role-file paths, shared guidance, bounded scope, protected state, checks, evidence, authority limits, and exact model and reasoning inheritance.
- Role creation occurs only after no existing valid role fits and only for a reusable role-definition gap; missing skills, tools, permissions, dependencies, or runtime capability stop with an exact diagnostic.

### Planned verification

- Map every delegated function to the existing Manage Sub-Agent Roles contract.
- Run existing-fit, reusable-gap, invalid-role, missing-skill, missing-tool, missing-permission, and inheritance-conflict scenarios.
- Verify no language bypasses fresh inventory or the Project Director's selection authority.

### Risks

- Solvers could receive materially different objectives and become incomparable.
- Parallel solvers could receive overlapping mutable write ownership.
- A default count could become a fixed global policy.

### Acceptance criteria

- The path is selected only when substantial uncertainty remains after decomposition analysis.
- Every solver receives the same bounded objective, governing evidence, scope, protected state, and stopping condition while its distinct role or perspective is explicit.
- Candidate outputs remain independent and reviewable, and solution development has no conflicting write ownership.
- The Director chooses two or more solvers proportionately unless a feasible user instruction fixes the count or roles.

### Planned verification

- Run an uncertain-nondecomposable scenario with at least two distinct solver profiles.
- Check delegation contracts for identical problem evidence and distinct perspectives.
- Check that candidate storage and write ownership remain independent.

## TASK-008 - Define one-to-one review and revision cycles

Add conditional formal review so each candidate has its own reviewer, rejected candidates return to their originating solver with actionable findings, revised candidates preserve prior records, and every revision is reviewed again before synthesis.

| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |

| Requirements | REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-022 |

| Dependencies | TASK-007 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-02T21:38:46.945396Z |

### Risks

- Reviewer assignments could be many-to-one or omit a candidate.
- Revision could overwrite prior evidence or route feedback to the wrong solver.
- Review loops could repeat without material change.

### Acceptance criteria

- The orchestration record contains one reviewer mapping for every candidate whenever formal review is selected.
- No unreviewed or rejected candidate enters synthesis, and a reviewer never takes Project Director ownership.
- A failed review preserves the candidate and review, returns clear findings to the originating solver, records a materially revised candidate, and repeats review.
- A repeated unchanged failure triggers the stopping contract instead of an endless loop.

### Planned verification

- Run a passing one-to-one review scenario and a mixed pass-fail scenario.
- Verify solver identity is preserved across rejection, revision, and re-review records.
- Run an unchanged-revision scenario and confirm it records a blocker rather than another identical cycle.

### Risks

- Synthesis could start before all reviews pass.
- The senior agent could silently discard a candidate or assume Director authority.
- Conflict recycling could omit an affected solver.

### Acceptance criteria

- The senior agent is distinct from the Project Director and receives every accepted candidate plus every material review finding.
- The integrated proposal preserves compatible contributions and explains resolved differences before returning to the Project Director.
- An irreconcilable conflict produces one exact shared conflict record delivered to every affected solver, followed by revised candidates, required reviews, and another synthesis attempt.
- A conflict that cannot progress reaches the truthful stopping path.

### Planned verification

- Run all-pass synthesis, resolvable-difference, irreconcilable-conflict, and no-progress conflict scenarios.
- Assert synthesis is gated on all required reviews and includes every accepted candidate and material finding.
- Verify every affected solver receives the same conflict explanation and returns through review.
